quiz.title: Module 2 — Understanding Content Strategy
quiz.description: Monday and Tuesday's combined quiz. It covers what a content strategy is and includes, choosing content pillars, and planning a calendar; then what the second video adds — how algorithms match content to viewers, on-target virality, staying consistent with one topic, picking the platform where your audience is, and building owned offers rather than relying on ads and brand deals.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of a content strategy for a brand or business?
options: To publish as many posts as possible every day
To copy the content strategies of successful competitors
To plan what content to create, how often to publish, and how it supports business goals
To focus exclusively on gaining followers
questions.explanation: A strategy answers what you make, how often, and why it matters to the goal. Volume, imitation and follower counts are all ways of avoiding that question.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an essential element of developing a content strategy?
options: Defining goals, understanding the audience, selecting content pillars, choosing platforms, and planning a content calendar
Posting on every social media platform regardless of available resources
Prioritising viral content without considering the target audience
Creating content without measuring its performance
questions.explanation: Those five decisions hang together: goals set direction, audience and pillars decide subject matter, and platform and calendar make it executable.

questions.prompt: A fitness coach wants to establish clear content pillars for their social media account. Which option best represents appropriate content pillars?
options: Monday, Wednesday, Friday, and Sunday
Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, and YouTube
Likes, comments, shares, and followers
Workout tips, nutrition advice, and client success stories
questions.explanation: Pillars are the recurring subjects you want to be known for. The other options are days, platforms and metrics — none of them describe what the content is about.

questions.prompt: According to the second video, what is the main way social media algorithms help creators grow?
options: By showing every post exclusively to existing followers
By matching content with viewers who are likely to find it interesting
By promoting accounts that publish the highest number of posts
By prioritising creators who use the most hashtags
questions.explanation: The algorithm is a matching system. It finds people who will engage with what you made, which is why clear, specific content travels further than volume.

questions.prompt: What does the second video mean by on-target virality?
options: Creating content that appeals equally to everyone on the internet
Trying to gain millions of views regardless of who watches
Reaching a large proportion of the specific audience a creator wants to attract
Publishing the same video on every available platform
questions.explanation: Reach among the wrong people does not build a brand. On-target virality means the audience you wanted saw it — which is what converts into opportunity.

questions.prompt: A content creator regularly posts about technology, fashion, sports, cooking, and finance on the same account, but wants to attract a specific audience interested in graphic design. Based on the second video, what should the creator do?
options: Focus consistently on graphic design content intended for the target audience
Continue posting about every topic to reach the widest possible audience
Stop using captions so the algorithm can decide the account's topic
Publish more frequently without changing the content topics
questions.explanation: A scattered account gives the audience and the algorithm no clear signal about who the content is for. Narrowing the focus is what makes the account findable.

questions.prompt: What does the second video recommend when choosing social media platforms for a business or creator who wants to grow effectively?
options: Establish a presence on every platform simultaneously
Focus only on the platform with the largest number of users
Move followers from one platform to another as frequently as possible
Focus on the platform where the target audience is most active and consistently create content there
questions.explanation: Growth comes from depth on the platform your audience already uses, not from thin presence everywhere or from the biggest user base in general.

questions.prompt: According to the second video, what is a more sustainable approach to making money from content than relying entirely on advertising revenue and brand deals?
options: Publishing viral videos without offering any products or services
Using content to attract attention and directing that attention toward owned products, services, or affiliate offers
Focusing exclusively on increasing follower counts
Creating content for as many unrelated audiences as possible
questions.explanation: Ad rates and sponsorships are outside your control. Pointing attention at something you own or earn from turns an audience into income you can sustain.
